sentences: Planes of colour in many different shapes overlap and lock together across the surface.

The Russian avant-garde artist Lyubov Popova joined Malevich's Suprematist group Supremus in 1916 and went on to paint a series she called Painterly Architectonics, to which this 1918 picture belongs.
As the word 'architectonic' suggests, she treated colour planes almost as solid building material, constructing a set of relationships in which each part props up or pushes against the others.
The series is seen as an attempt to join Malevich's geometric colour planes with the relief constructions of Vladimir Tatlin, in whose Moscow studio she worked around 1912.
Born into a wealthy textile merchant's family, she studied with Cubist painters in Paris in 1912–1913, and she was deeply drawn to ancient Russian icons and the paintings of Giotto.
In 1921, with fellow artists, she declared easel painting finished and committed herself to applied arts such as textile design.
In 1924 she died of scarlet fever, caught from her son, just two days after his death; she was thirty-five.
